name: Asphodel
classification_notes: Letters link into a single continuous line rather than sitting as independent glyphs, closer to a logotype system than a conventional text script, which places it in the script category.
summary: A free connected display face where letters link into a single flowing line, built for logotype-style compositions.
description: Asphodel joins its letters into a single continuous line, closer to a logotype system than a conventional script. It ships as one free style with discretionary ligatures, case-sensitive forms and swash variants for the initial, capital and terminal positions.
foundry_blurb: Alexandre Créquer lists Asphodel's features as discretionary ligatures, case-sensitive forms, initial, capital and terminal swashes, and a standard ampersand variant.

name: Ring
classification_notes: A bold, rounded grotesque with squared dots and alternate R and K forms, read as sans-serif rather than display given its full seven-weight text-style range.
summary: A rounded grotesque in seven weights with matching italics, built with squared dots and a handful of playful alternates.
description: Ring is a bold, rounded sans running from Thin to Black with a matching italic at every weight. Alternate R and K forms and squared dots give it a bit of personality without disturbing its general-purpose grotesque structure.
foundry_blurb: Alexandre Créquer lists Ring's features as discretionary ligatures, case-sensitive forms, alternate R, alternate K and k, and squared dots, across 14 styles.

name: Mosa
classification_notes: Wide circular letterforms and sharply cut diagonals built for caps-forward display use, in the geometric sans tradition.
summary: A geometric caps-forward sans in five weights, with a diagonal-cut M and A that give its wordmarks a distinct silhouette.
description: Mosa is a geometric sans running from Thin to Black, built around wide circular letterforms and sharply cut diagonals. Alternate A, E and F forms plus thin punctuation and diacritics round out the set.
foundry_blurb: Alexandre Créquer notes Mosa's discretionary ligatures, thin punctuation and diacritics, and alternate A, and E and F forms.

name: Large
classification_notes: Pronounced thick-thin stroke contrast and old style figures place it as an elegant high-contrast display serif rather than a text face.
summary: A high-contrast display serif with old style figures, built for elegant headline and logotype work.
description: Large is a single-weight display serif with pronounced contrast between thick and thin strokes, paired with a companion italic. Old style figures, case-sensitive forms and an alternate Q add refinement to what is otherwise a spare, elegant letter.
foundry_blurb: Alexandre Créquer lists Large's features as discretionary ligatures, old style figures, case-sensitive forms and an alternate Q, across regular and italic.

name: Sagace
classification_notes: Heavy flared wedge serifs across a full weight range place it as a bold display serif built for confident headline use.
summary: A bold wedge-serif display face in five weights with matching italics, built for confident headline work.
description: Sagace is a display serif with heavy, flared wedge serifs, running from Thin to Bold with a matching italic at every weight. Alternate a, g, r and Q forms and case-sensitive figures give it room for customisation in logotype use.
foundry_blurb: Alexandre Créquer notes Sagace's discretionary ligatures, case-sensitive forms and alternate glyphs for a, g, r and Q, across 10 styles.

name: Pouler
classification_notes: Thick, faintly irregular strokes and quirky curved terminals on an all-caps single style place it as a playful display face rather than a workhorse text font.
summary: A free, bold all-caps display face with chunky, slightly irregular strokes built for posters and short headlines.
description: Pouler is a single-weight, all-caps display face with thick, faintly wobbly strokes and quirky curved terminals. It ships free, with discretionary ligatures as its one OpenType feature.
foundry_blurb: Alexandre Créquer notes Pouler for its discretionary ligatures.

name: Aukera
classification_notes: A single-weight geometric display face offering alternate characters rather than a weight range, placed as sans-serif given no serif detailing is described.
summary: A free single-weight display face with alternate A, C, E, F and Q forms for quick customisation.
description: Aukera is a free, single-weight display face offering discretionary ligatures and alternate characters for A, C, E, F and Q, giving it some flexibility in logotype and short-text settings.
foundry_blurb: Alexandre Créquer notes Aukera as a free font with discretionary ligatures and alternate characters for A, C, E, F and Q.
